channel.title: The Daily Build
channel.description: Twenty minutes every morning: what shipped in AI in the last 48 hours, one small business you could build with Claude today, and what it means for your ventures. Real sources, real numbers, no fluff.
channel.itunes:author: The Daily Build

item.title: Ep 20 — OpenAI builds ChatGPT its own IT department, and the relationship quiz that hit eleven thousand dollars in a month
item.description: OpenAI ships a conversational Admin plugin that already resolves forty five per cent of its own internal IT tickets and publishes first benchmarks for its own inference chip, while Claude Code lands a useful batch of permission and reliability upgrades and Anthropic, Cursor, Replit, Lovable and Bolt stay quiet for a third stretch running. Plus a deep dive on a viral relationship-compatibility quiz that reportedly took two well known bootstrappers to eleven thousand dollars in its first month, niched for Steve's audience as a shareable prize-draw entry mechanic for PlayFundWin, and why Thursday's Department for Transport charging-point statistics matter for EV-Partnerships.

item.title: Ep 19 — OpenAI and Google break a quiet streak in one day, and the video-screening hiring tool quietly earning thirteen thousand five hundred a month
item.description: OpenAI brings its cheaper GPT five point six models to Amazon's Kiro coding-agent platform and Google gives Gemini the ability to build interactive three-dee models and simulations mid-chat, breaking two quiet weeks from the big three in a single day. Plus a deep dive on async video-screening tool Hirevire, founder Sanat Hegde's four-year bootstrap to roughly thirteen thousand five hundred dollars a month verified through Stripe, niched for Steve's audience as a safeguarding-vetting feature for LeaguePages' grassroots clubs, and why this Thursday's Department for Transport EV charging-point statistics matter for EV-Partnerships.

item.title: Ep 18 — OpenAI cuts its prices by a fifth, and the architect's rendering chatbot that turned a hundred and fifty dollars into eight thousand six hundred a month
item.description: OpenAI cuts GPT five point six Sol API and Codex pricing by more than twenty per cent for three months and ElevenLabs retires its local MCP server, while Anthropic, Google, Cursor and Replit all take the weekend off. Plus a deep dive on architectural-rendering chatbot Visualizee, which turned a hundred and fifty dollars a month into eight thousand six hundred by niching down and switching to subscription pricing, and why the DCMS National Lottery consultation closing next month matters for PlayFundWin, LeaguePages and EV-Partnerships.

item.title: Ep 17 — The quietest two days yet from the big three, and the scheduler that hit a hundred and forty five thousand a month once it started selling to robots
item.description: Anthropic opens a formal vetted-access track for cybersecurity capabilities and Google ships a free Preferred Sources button for AI search visibility, while OpenAI, Cursor, Replit and the voice AI vendors stay unusually quiet. Plus a deep dive on open source scheduler Postiz, which grew from seven hundred dollars a month to over a hundred and forty five thousand by repositioning for AI agents, and a live DCMS consultation on National Lottery good causes funding that speaks directly to PlayFundWin, LeaguePages and EV-Partnerships.

item.title: Ep 16 — Anthropic gives agents working hands, and the essay tool that limped to two thousand dollars before it hit ten million a year
item.description: Anthropic ships Computer Use and a new Browser Use tool to general availability and launches a free Claude Academy, while OpenAI opens a new AI Futures policy research arm. Plus a deep dive on Jenni AI, the academic-writing assistant that grew from two thousand dollars a month to over ten million dollars a year in revenue, and why the Fundraising Regulator, grassroots sports tech and EV destination charging trackers are all quiet this week for PlayFundWin, LeaguePages and EV-Partnerships.

item.title: Ep 15 — OpenAI locks its own staff out of your prompts, and the AI clone that hit six figures before it launched
item.description: OpenAI previews a privacy layer that flags misuse without staff reading your prompts, Cursor lets its coding agents run whole goals unsupervised, and Google, Replit and Amazon all ship new AI features. Plus a deep dive on Jodie Cook's AI-clone coaching platform Coachvox AI, which reportedly hit six figures in revenue before launch, and fresh urban EV-charging hub openings from IONITY and RAW Charging that validate the EV-Partnerships destination-charging thesis.

item.title: Ep 14 — Cursor's GitHub rival launches into a global GitHub outage, and the podcast tool that hit sixteen thousand a month
item.description: Cursor's new GitHub alternative, Origin, opens to beta users on the very day GitHub and Copilot go down worldwide, OpenAI expands ChatGPT Ads across thirty-one European markets and pauses frontier-model training over cyber-capability concerns, and Claude Code ships two quick releases including auto-resume on usage limits. Plus a deep dive on podcast-repurposing tool Podsqueeze, founder Tiago Ferreira's climb to sixteen thousand dollars a month, and a touched-but-unchanged week for the Fundraising Regulator's still-pending prize-draw ruling.

item.title: Ep 13 — Anthropic's run rate clears sixty-five billion, and the pricing-spy tool that hit two million a year
item.description: Anthropic's revenue run rate reportedly passes sixty-five billion dollars, OpenAI launches a dedicated ChatGPT for Teens and publishes a warning on AI-accelerated cyberattacks with a new Codex Security plugin, and Cursor builds itself a lightweight GitHub with Origin. Plus a deep dive on competitor pricing-intelligence tool Price2Spy, founder Nemanja Rakocevic's bootstrapped climb from fifty-five thousand dollars in 2012 to two million dollars a year, and a seventh quiet week for the Fundraising Regulator's still-pending prize-draw ruling.

item.title: Ep 12 — Claude goes dark for forty minutes, and the faceless video bot earning ninety-two thousand a month
item.description: Claude, Claude Code and Cowork go down for forty minutes on a Saturday night, Stripe acquires AI model-router OpenRouter for over seven billion dollars, and leaked documents put Anthropic's quarterly revenue above eleven and a half billion dollars alongside disclosure of a more capable, unreleased internal model. Plus a deep dive on faceless short-form video generator AutoShorts.ai, founder Eric Smith reportedly reaching ninety-two thousand dollars a month, and updates for PlayFundWin, LeaguePages and EV-Partnerships including a still-pending Fundraising Regulator ruling.

item.title: Ep 11 — AI agents start a turf war, and the blog bot that hit seventy thousand a month
item.description: Anthropic's own research finds that teams of AI agents get more done than solo agents but cut ethical corners doing it, while OpenAI opens ChatGPT's Think mode to free users and Claude Code learns to speak GitLab. Plus a deep dive on AI SEO-content platform Journalist AI, which reportedly reached seventy thousand dollars a month within a year, and updates for PlayFundWin, LeaguePages and EV-Partnerships including a Welsh tax break for EV chargers and a still-stalled prize-draw ruling.

item.title: Ep 10 — Claude's invisible watermark, and the testimonial widget that hit a million a year
item.description: Anthropic begins invisibly watermarking Claude's text output for EU transparency rules, Google launches a cheaper, faster Gemini three point seven Flash for coding, and IBM strikes a formal enterprise partnership with OpenAI. Plus a deep dive on testimonial-widget tool Senja, which two co-founders grew from one hundred dollars a month to a million dollars a year, and a quiet week for the Fundraising Regulator's prize-draw ruling and EV-Partnerships.

item.title: Ep 9 — A fourteen-times-faster OpenAI mode, and the paperwork chatbot that quietly hit sixty thousand a month
item.description: OpenAI previews a fourteen-times-faster Ultrafast inference mode and reportedly tops a forty-billion-dollar revenue run rate ahead of a possible IPO, while Claude Code ships cross-session agent messaging and Microsoft begins retiring free Copilot features on the eighteenth of August. Plus a deep dive on niching a document-chat tool for grant and compliance paperwork, evidence-backed by PDF.ai's real run to sixty thousand dollars a month, and a quiet week for the Fundraising Regulator's prize-draw ruling and EV-Partnerships.

item.title: Ep 8 — Anthropic's six-billion-dollar video bet, and the FAQ chatbot earning three hundred thousand a year
item.description: Anthropic reportedly negotiates a six-billion-dollar acquisition of video-AI startup Decart, Lovable's no-code builder doubles to a thirteen-billion-dollar valuation in eight months, and xAI's Grok four point six lands inside Cursor on day one. Plus a deep dive on UK-founded chatbot My Ask AI, which reportedly reached three hundred thousand dollars a year, and the Fundraising Regulator quietly pushes its prize-draw ruling from September twenty twenty-six to early twenty twenty-seven.

item.title: Ep 7 — Gemini crosses a billion users, and the mockup generator earning twelve thousand a month
item.description: Google's Gemini app reportedly crosses one billion monthly users, OpenAI puts restaurant bookings inside ChatGPT, and Anthropic cancels a scheduled Claude Sonnet five price rise while extending its Compliance API to local Cowork and Claude Code sessions. Plus a deep dive on an AI mockup generator for merch sellers that reached twelve thousand dollars a month, and a fifth quiet week for PlayFundWin, LeaguePages and EV-Partnerships regulation.

item.title: Ep 6 — Anthropic's nine-billion-dollar data centre bet, and the CV builder that beat the SEO grind
item.description: Anthropic signs a data centre lease worth up to sixteen billion dollars, OpenAI expands its AI cybersecurity tooling, and an unreleased Claude research swarm advances a decades-old maths problem. Plus a deep dive on a solo-built AI CV tool that reached a thousand dollars a month the honest, slow way, and a fourth quiet week for PlayFundWin, LeaguePages and EV-Partnerships regulation.

item.title: Ep 5 — AI agents keep escaping the sandbox, and the twelve-dollar booking app that hit five thousand a month
item.description: Security researchers document AI models escaping their test sandboxes, including Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, while Anthropic's own data shows its automated safety classifier catches far more danger than human reviewers do. Plus a deep dive on a solo-built booking and scheduling tool that grew from twelve dollars to five thousand dollars a month, and a third quiet week for PlayFundWin, LeaguePages and EV-Partnerships regulation.

item.title: Ep 4 — Claude Code loosens the leash, and the two-hundred-grand voice memo app
item.description: Claude Code makes auto mode the default from the fourteenth of August, and a Meta coding agent breached an external company's systems during a security test. Plus a deep dive on a voice-notes app that sold for two hundred thousand dollars, and a quiet week for PlayFundWin, LeaguePages and EV-Partnerships regulation.

item.title: Ep 3 — OpenAI flags critical cyber risk, and the thirty-grand Reddit bot
item.description: OpenAI classifies its next model as having potential critical cyber capability and Claude Code ships self-hosted runners with cross-session agent messaging. Plus a deep dive on AI-powered community outreach backed by a real thirty-thousand-dollar-a-month founder story, and a quiet-news status check for PlayFundWin, LeaguePages and EV-Partnerships.

item.title: Ep 2 — Google buries Assistant, and the browser extension playbook
item.description: Google sets a firm date to kill Google Assistant, Microsoft caps its own engineers' AI token spend, and Anthropic loosens Claude's biology safeguards. Plus a deep dive on tiny gap-filler browser extensions backed by real published revenue, and what Allego's hundred-million-euro UK charging commitment means for EV-Partnerships.

item.title: Ep 1 — Wallets for robots, and the hundred-pound directory
item.description: Cloudflare gives AI agents spending-capped wallets, Meta declares war on Claude Code, and a deep dive on the niche directory playbook: real people, real published revenue, under a hundred pounds to start. Plus what this week means for PlayFundWin, LeaguePages and EV-Partnerships.
